newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says policy to keep aiming to support recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says policy to keep aiming to support recovery.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday that the central bank will continue to conduct its monetary policy with the aim of strengthening the basis for economic recovery.

Matsushita told a news conference although Japan's economy continues to be affected by a rise in the sales tax in April, the economy as a whole is continuing to recover gradually and this was confirmed by a meeting of BOJ branch managers this week.
"For the time being we will continue to carry out monetary policy putting emphasis on economic recovery," Matsushita said.
He said both public investment and housing investment continued to be on a declining trend but added that production and incomes remained firm.

He also said that Japan's net exports were rising sharply, and this was a factor supporting the economy. But he said the impact of the April 1 sales tax rise, especially on private consumption, had been larger than expected.
"The decline in private consumption in reaction to the tax rise is a bit more prolonged (than expected)," he said.
Matsushita said that due to an improvement in employment conditions, including wages, the underlying recovery trend in private consumption was unlikely to falter.
He said it became evident in the two-day meeting of BOJ branch managers that the tempo of recovery in smaller to medium-sized firms, especially non-manufacturers, was flagging.
He added that these firms had been hit by the fall in public works spending and a decrease in private consumption arising from the sales tax rise.
But at the same time, business conditions at manufacturers, including some smaller to medium-sized firms, were improving, supported by strong exports.

Matsushita said that, looking at the economy as a whole, a positive mechanism was at work, adding: "The current economic slowdown will be temporary and it is highly likely that the economic recovery will continue."
But Matsushita said the two-day branch managers meeting earlier this week failed to provide the central bank with enough evidence to convince it that the tempo of the recovery would gain strength.
He added that the central bank would continue to closely watch future economic movements.
Matsushita also said there was no large gap between the central bank and the Japanese government in their assessments of the economy.

"In its assessment of the economy the government has said that the pace of recovery will be gradual temporarily. In that sense there is no large gap between that and (the assessment) of the BOJ," Matsushita said.

In its latest monthly economic report, the government's Economic Planning Agency took "half a step" forward in its assessment of the economy. The agency's report said: "Although the tempo of the recovery has temporarily slowed down, the economy is continuing to recover, centring on firm private demand."
